summary:
After landing, astronauts' balance is at its worst just when they must leave the vehicle. NASA's recovery model for 37 ISS crew estimates an eyes-closed balance score of 13.2 at landing, against 74.9 before flight, and crew are at increased risk of falls and injury during readaptation. On the Moon or Mars, no ground recovery team will be present,
so the crew must judge readiness on site.

We developed the Gravity-Transition Readiness Model, a browser-based prototype that converts a short standing-balance test on a force plate into an explicit egress recommendation (GO, CAUTION, NO-GO or CANNOT ASSESS). Each result names the rule that produced it. When a valid test without a fall falls short of GO, the model estimates when to retest, using NASA crew recovery data (Wood et al. 2015) and NASA's definition of recovery (Jain et al. 2010).

The model is deterministic and traceable to cited sources, and it supports the crew surgeon's decision; it does not constitute clearance. Its thresholds have not yet been validated against egress outcomes.
details:
What it does:

The application assesses whether a crew member can leave the vehicle after landing and, if not, when balance should be retested. The user enters the crew member's preflight baseline, the time since landing and the result of a standing-balance test in four sensory conditions. The model returns GO, CAUTION, NO-GO or CANNOT ASSESS, states the rule that produced the result and recommends the next action.

How it works:

Each 20-s trial on a force plate is converted into the equilibrium score used by NASA and expressed as a share of the crew member's own baseline. Seven numbered rules are applied in a fixed order. A fall or a score below 75% of baseline gives NO-GO, following NASA's definition of recovery (Jain et al. 2010). An overall GO requires two GO sessions at least 2 h apart. When a valid test without a fall falls short of GO, the NASA recovery model for 37 ISS crew (Wood et al. 2015) estimates when to retest, anchored on the measured deficit. In the worked example, a crew member who is NO-GO 6 h after landing is advised to retest in about 63 h (range 25 to 110 h).

Benefits and intended impact:

During readaptation, crew members are at increased risk of falls and have reduced ability to control vehicles. Injuries have probably occurred but have not been recorded systematically (Jain et al. 2010). On the Moon or Mars, no ground recovery team will be present. The model gives the crew and the crew surgeon an explicit, documented recommendation and a personal retest time. It supports their decision and does not constitute clearance.

Creativity:

The project combines NASA findings that are usually reported separately into one traceable decision rule and a personal retest time. At the same 6 h, a deficit half, equal to or 1.5 times the typical value gives retest estimates of about 35, 63 and 110 h, whereas the average curve alone gives one time. No dataset labelled with egress outcomes was found in the sources searched, so no classifier is trained and every threshold is cited.

Evaluation and limitations:

Healthy adults aged 25 to 55 from the public HBEDB dataset (n = 43) score 94.1 and 92.9 on firm floor with eyes open and closed, against NASA crew preflight means of 94.3 and 89.9. Of 140 reference participants, 42.9% return GO in a single test, because the rules are designed to favour retesting. 201 automated tests verify the rules, the retest solver and the application. The participants are not astronauts, post-landing sessions are simulated, the recovery model is unvalidated for the Moon or Mars, and the thresholds have not been validated against egress outcomes.

Factors considered:

Safety (a fall overrides any score and testing requires a spotter or harness), explainability, learning effects in baseline testing, tolerability of testing on landing day, and transfer from Earth to other gravity levels.

Tools. Python, Streamlit, NumPy, SciPy, pandas and Plotly. The app runs entirely in the browser through stlite on GitHub Pages, so it needs no server. Documentation uses MkDocs Material. No hardware was built.
